_label: Evidence archive: documentation photographs of the Ansel Adams print (August 2008)

identified_by.content: Evidence archive: documentation photographs of the Ansel Adams print (August 2008)

content: Sun & Rain Works holds eleven digital photographs, taken in a single session on 2008-08-08, that document a matted black-and-white photographic print in the studio's possession. The sequence records the print recto, the mount, the verso with its backing and hanging wire, and a close-up of the verso credit block. In one frame the print is photographed together with a copy of Andy Warhol's 'The Philosophy of Andy Warhol (From A to B and Back Again)', placed upright and facing the camera. The close-up of the verso shows a printed credit block reading 'Photograph by Ansel Adams for The American Trust Company', a negative number beginning '1-SF-', the beginning of a handwritten title 'San Francisco fr...', and a hand-inked annotation 'Wells Fargo Bank' written over the struck-through word 'THE'. These markings correspond, in four independent particulars, to the markings recorded in the public Sotheby's catalogue entry for lot 16 of Photographs, sale N08533 (2009) - the Ansel Adams print 'San Francisco from Twin Peaks'. The photographs therefore evidence that a print bearing the markings described in the lot-16 catalogue entry was in the studio's possession nearly eight months before that sale of 30 March 2009, and that it was documented there alongside an art-referential object. They do not establish the identity of the consignor of record, and they establish no precedence over any later artist, work, or event.

referred_to_by.content: Evidence status: independently checkable. Unlike the studio's correspondence and receipts, this record can be tested by any third party without access to private material. The public Sotheby's catalogue entry for sale N08533, lot 16, at https://www.sothebys.com/en/auctions/ecatalogue/2009/photographs-n08533/lot.16.html describes the print as carrying the photographer's 'Photograph by Ansel Adams for The American Trust Company' stamp, as numbered 1-SF-46, as titled, and as annotated 'Wells Fargo Bank' in ink on the reverse by the photographer; the catalogue note explains the annotation as Adams's own correction following the 1960 merger of The American Trust Company into Wells Fargo Bank. Each of those particulars is visible in the studio's 2008 verso photograph, which is published with this record, except that the negative number is legible only as far as '1-SF-' before the right edge of the frame cuts it off; the catalogue's '46' is therefore not visible and is not claimed here. A vertical crease runs through the mount to the left of the number but does not obscure it. The correspondence is therefore in four particulars - the credit stamp, the negative-number series, the inked Wells Fargo annotation over the struck-through article, and the handwritten title - and is not dependent on the studio's own account.

Embedded image metadata, as recorded by the camera: all eleven files carry Exif written at capture by a FUJIFILM FinePix1300, reporting the firmware string 'Digital Camera FinePix1300 Ver1.24'. Exif DateTimeOriginal values run from 2008-08-08 00:05:33 to 2008-08-08 00:10:22, a continuous session of under five minutes. The frames are numbered DSCF0012 to DSCF0017 and DSCF0020 to DSCF0024; frames 0018 and 0019 are absent from the sequence. This metadata is written by the camera at exposure and is independent of the filesystem timestamps of the storage medium, which agree with it. It remains studio-held and is not notarized: no checksums, file hashes, or custody identifiers are published at this time, and Exif fields can in principle be altered.

Contemporaneous conceptual intent. One frame in the sequence, exposed at 2008-08-08 00:08:46, shows the print photographed together with a copy of 'The Philosophy of Andy Warhol (From A to B and Back Again)', stood upright and facing the camera on the same ground. Sun & Rain Works reads this juxtaposition as a deliberate art-referential gesture made at the time of documentation, and as the earliest dated trace of the thinking that became The Auction as Artwork. The scope of that reading should be stated plainly: the photograph evidences that the two objects were deliberately composed in one frame in August 2008. It is not a written designation, it does not by itself establish that the auction engagement was framed as art in 2008 or 2009, and the conceptual designation remains an assertion by the artist made explicit over time.

Limits of the correspondence. Ansel Adams produced multiple prints from the 1952 negative, so agreement on the verso markings identifies a print of the same issue and annotation state rather than establishing a unique object beyond question; the strength of the match rests on the combination of particulars, not on any one of them. The photographs show that the print was in the room in which they were taken; the attribution of that room and camera to Sun & Rain Works rests on the studio's custody of the storage medium. The Sotheby's catalogue names no consignor, as is standard auction practice, so the identity of the consignor of record is not established by these photographs. It is evidenced separately: the consignment correspondence record carries two messages of March 2009 in which the auction house's own Photographs department writes to the studio principal about 'your photograph' and chases the signed consignment agreement it had posted in February.

Corroborated from outside the files. The eleven frames described here were transmitted as a zip attachment to Sotheby's on 2008-08-14, six days after exposure, and that attachment is held: its twelve entries are byte-for-byte identical to the studio's loose copies, and its Info-ZIP UNIX extra fields carry Unix-epoch modification times of 2008-08-08 07:05:36Z to 07:10:24Z. The covering message describes the photographs as made with a 1.3 megapixel FujiFilm camera, which agrees with the FinePix1300 named in the Exif and with the 1280 by 960 frame size. The caveat recorded above, that Exif fields can in principle be altered, should now be read against that agreement. One frame in the set, DSCF0020, is the frame composing the print with Warhol's philosophy; it was among those sent. See the 2008 approach record.

referred_to_by.content: The eleven frames are also held as loose files, and their two clocks agree. Besides the archive San Francisco.zip, the studio holds the eleven photographs as individual files carrying filesystem timestamps. Those timestamps run from 23:05:36 to 23:10:24 on 2008-08-07, while the EXIF DateTimeOriginal values of the same files run from 00:05:33 to 00:10:22 on 2008-08-08. The difference is constant, between fifty-nine minutes fifty-seven seconds and fifty-nine minutes fifty-eight seconds across the set, and the intervals between successive frames are the same in both series. This does not re-date the session, and an earlier reading of it that did has been discarded. Every filesystem timestamp falls on an even second, which is the two-second granularity of the FAT file system used by camera cards, and FAT stores local time with no timezone, so the same stored value is read an hour out when the reading system applies different daylight-saving rules. A one-hour offset between a FAT timestamp and an EXIF value is therefore the expected artefact of reading the card later and elsewhere, not evidence that either clock was wrong. What the agreement does establish is worth having on its own. The two series track each other frame for frame, so the session was a single unbroken run of about five minutes rather than an assembly from several occasions; and the files carry card timestamps at all, which means they were preserved from the camera card rather than re-saved by later software. The session date this collection uses remains the EXIF date, 2008-08-08, which is the camera's own record of its own exposure.

A second photograph of the verso, from a different camera, showing the whole inscription. The close-up published with this record as images/adams-verso-2008.jpg is a frame from the session of 2008-08-08, and it is cropped: it carries the credit block and the inked 'Wells Fargo Bank' annotation, but its right edge cuts off the negative number after '1-SF-' and cuts the handwritten title off after 'San Francisco fr'. The studio also holds a photograph of the same verso made with a different camera, an Olympus C3100Z, in which the whole inscription is within the frame and legible: the printed block 'PHOTOGRAPH BY ANSEL ADAMS FOR THE AMERICAN TRUST COMPANY' with 'THE' struck through and 'Wells Fargo Bank' written in by hand, an empty 'NO.' line, 'NEGATIVE No. 1-SF-46', and beneath it, in the same hand, 'San Francisco from Twin Peaks'. It is published here as images/adams-verso-full-2008.jpg. Every element it shows is already independently attested by the public auction catalogue entry for lot 16 of sale N08533, which records the stamp, the number 1-SF-46, the title and the Wells Fargo annotation; the photograph adds legibility, not a new fact. That frame is not a stray file. It is one of a series of seventeen already recorded in this collection as the staged photographs of the print, where all seventeen are enumerated and the two verso frames are noted; what is new here is that one of them is published, so the whole inscription can be read rather than described.

A correction to this record, about the date of that frame. An earlier version of this passage said the frame carried no reliable date, that a filesystem timestamp of 2009-01-20 was all that remained, and that no date was asserted for the series. That was wrong on every count, and it was written without consulting the record that already covers these files. The staged-photographs record dates the series to autumn 2008 by a three-part analysis which is stronger than anything offered here. Its floor is independent of any clock: the files were rewritten by QuickTime 7.5.5 running on Mac OS X 10.5.5, released on 2008-09-09 and 2008-09-15, so they cannot have been processed by that pairing before the middle of September 2008. Its middle term is the processing time those rewrites left, 2008-11-25 between 18:56:10 and 18:56:17 in frame order. And the 2009-01-20 timestamp cited in the earlier version of this passage is in that record too, correctly, as the ceiling rather than the date: it is the file system's record of the copy into the studio's working folder, not of the capture or the processing. That record also explains the file names, which this one did not: an Olympus that has never had its clock set reports 1 January, and builds 'P101' out of it. The date of capture itself remains unestablished, as it says. Nothing in that analysis is displaced by the copies from which the published frame was taken, whose own timestamps are a property of the copying and carry no weight.
